sources.title: FAO1998 — painted spiny-lobster diagnosis and comparative figures
sources.scope: Actual selected PDFpage48 printed1013 Fig20f and PDFpage56 printed1021 species figure/diagnosis viewed. Four separated principal plate spines without extra spinules, tapered antennae, non-chelate P1–4 and body/pigment layout guide this unmeasured reconstruction. Smooth abdomen distinguished from shallow pubescent fields2/3. Not a full-volume review or fitted morphology.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected actual PDF text and rendered figures

sources.title: Smithsonian SERC NEMESIS — Panulirus versicolor
sources.scope: Selected species-account morphology read. Institutional account, not a Smithsonian collection determination. No source photo borrowed from this account; the retained OpenCage licensed image is separate.

findings.shape: A separately proportioned spiny carapace, four separated principal antennular-plate spines, longer antennules, strong tapered second antennae, smooth six-somite banded abdomen with shallow selected pubescent-area cues on somites2/3, five-part fan and ten articulated non-chelate limbs replace the generic draft.
findings.surface: An original irregular blue-green and pale cuticle mosaic, pale abdominal bands with dark margins, longitudinal pale/dark leg stripes, selected pink basal antennae with pale flagella, and original fan-ray cues follow the retained OpenCage photograph and scoped FAO descriptions.
findings.movement: The same retained surfaces perform a short supported forward bout, antenna/antennule articulation, partial search gesture, quiet support and mild serial tail/fan flex. No great Homarus claws, measured locomotor sequence, escape displacement, food interaction, stridulation or physiological sensing is claimed.
findings.evidenceScope: The authentic OpenCage CC BY-SA2.5 photograph and selected actual Naturalis/FAO and Smithsonian SERC account diagnoses were compared. Actual FAO1998 PDFpage48 printed1013 Fig20f and page56 printed1021 species illustration/diagnosis were rendered/viewed. Smithsonian account morphology is distinguished from a collection determination; the photograph comes from OpenCage, not SERC. Shallow pubescent areas are distinguished from transverse grooves, and adult/juvenile color descriptions are scoped.
corrections: Replaced oversized cream patches with a finer irregular cellular mosaic and refined its scale after the top-view comparison.
Kept the four principal antennular-plate spines and smooth banded abdomen distinct from the European form.
Thickened visibly wire-like walking segments while retaining fixed lengths and longitudinal streaks.
Moved eye ends beyond the carapace, tapered antennae/horns and reduced artificial frontal/mouth panels.
Completed final lifted recovery before stopping, kept planted toes fixed and attached anatomy markers to the actual carapace, antenna base and moving fan.
findings.residual: Exact body ratios, principal/secondary spine positions, pubescent fields and setae, fan/pleopod membranes, antennal articulation and mouthparts remain approximate. Original pigment and roughness are not measured cuticle optics or a scan. Source-photo stage/sex are not independently redetermined. Female P5 chelation, internal anatomy, true sensory processing, stridulation, food handling/ingestion and hydrodynamic escape are absent. The model remains partly stylized, with authored unmeasured support and partial tail articulation rather than validated biological biomechanics.
